headline: Shrink every qualifying positive window
statement: Given positive integers nums and positive target, return the minimum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target. Return zero when no such subarray exists.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Keep a continuous group of numbers and its sum. Add a number on the right until the sum reaches the target. Then remove numbers from the left while the sum still qualifies. Positive inputs make this safe: removing a number always reduces the sum.
approach: Extend right and add nums[right] to total.
While total>=target, update the best length and remove nums[left].
Translate an untouched best sentinel into zero.
correctness: While processing right, total=sum(nums[left:right+1]). For a fixed right endpoint, successive shrinking examines every qualifying left boundary until positivity makes the sum too small. Discarded left boundaries can never give a shorter solution with a later right endpoint. Thus every possible globally shortest window is considered.
bruteForce: Try every start and end while accumulating sums, using O(n^2) time.

complexity.explanation: Each pointer advances at most n times, so the nested while loop is linear in total.

pitfalls: Update best before removing a left value.
This window strategy relies on strictly positive values.
